Subagent orchestration gate
Result: use-subagent-orchestrator
Reason: Strong orchestration signals detected (debugging/root-cause, multi-surface scope, tests/verification).
Action: Production contract: invoke the subagent-orchestrator skill before broad work; choose single-thread, sequential-plan, or parallel-subagents; if parallel-subagents is selected and tool policy permits, emit a compact why-parallel proof, define bounded roles, spawn the smallest useful bounded read-only roster, wait, then synthesize before edits; if tool policy requires explicit user authorization before spawning, ask the user whether to spawn subagents; if spawning is otherwise unavailable or blocked, state the blocker and continue with the closest safe fallback.

Why parallel:
- independent track 1: map API, worker, and database failure surfaces and changed files
- independent track 2: identify flaky CI reproduction paths, test gaps, and verification commands
Blockers checked: explicit user opt-out, child-agent recursion, strict sequential dependencies, conflicting writes, workspace-write dirty-state isolation, external side effects, privacy/tool limits, unbounded broad agent tasks.
Read-only agents must report whether findings depend on uncommitted changes.
Subagents:
- so_mapper
  mode: read-only
  scope: API, worker, and database failure surfaces
  expected output: files, hypotheses, uncertainty, and report whether findings depend on uncommitted changes
  constraints: no recursive fan-out
- so_tester
  mode: read-only
  scope: flaky CI reproduction paths and missing tests
  expected output: targeted checks, coverage gaps, and report whether findings depend on uncommitted changes
  constraints: no recursive fan-out
